text:
acme_integration: Hey @support_jess — since the 2/12 deploy we're seeing invalid JSON from the API when using structured JSON output. The response sometimes has partial objects in the items array and an unexpected "metadata" key that breaks our downstream parser. Repro + payload below.

support_jess: thanks — can you paste the exact request and the raw response you received? any request_id/region/model info helps.

acme_integration: here's the call we make (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"list items","response_format":{"type":"json","schema":{"items":[{"id":"string","name":"string","value":"number"}]}},"stream":true}'
```
and the raw response body we got (from our proxy logs):
```json
{"items":[{"id":"a1","name":"foo","value":12},{"name":"bar","value":7},{"id":"a3","name":"baz","value":5,"metadata":{"source":"heuristic"}}]}
```
Our JSON parser fails on the second array item because "id" is missing, and then the extra "metadata" on the third item is not in our schema. We only see this intermittently (~5% of requests) and started after your 2/12 model refresh.

support_jess: got it. two quick clarifying q's: (1) do you see this only with `stream=true`? (2) can you share a request_id from one of the failing calls?

acme_integration: yes — most failures correlate with streaming true. example request_id: req_20230212_9f3b. Region: us-west-2. Model: rwd-3b-v2.

eng_runtime_lee: thanks @acme_integration and @support_jess. Streaming can produce chunks that split objects if the model emits in pieces; robust clients should reassemble chunks before JSON parsing. Two immediate asks: try the same call with "stream":false and see if you still get malformed JSON, and attach the raw chunk sequence if possible.

acme_integration: tried `stream=false` and the problem disappeared in our quick smoke test (same inputs). I also pulled the raw chunk log for req_20230212_9f3b — here's the sequence (reconstructed):
```
chunk 1: {"items":[{"id":"a1","name":"foo","value":12},
chunk 2: {"name":"bar","value":7},
chunk 3: {"id":"a3","name":"baz","value":5,"metadata":{"source":"heuristic"}}]}
```
So chunk 2 starts mid-object (the model didn't include the id in that chunk), so our proxy tried to parse each chunk as standalone JSON and failed.

eng_runtime_lee: that confirms a streaming boundary reassembly issue. Our streaming guarantees are best-effort for token boundaries; we don't guarantee chunk-level object completeness. Recommended mitigations:
- Reassemble the full stream (concatenate chunks) before JSON parse, or buffer until you receive a closing `]}` for the top-level array.
- If you need chunk-level parsing, add an envelope in the prompt so each item is emitted as a self-contained JSON object per line (e.g., `\n###ITEM###\n` separators) so chunk-splitting is less likely to produce invalid JSON.

acme_integration: ok that's helpful. two follow-ups: (1) what about the unexpected `metadata` key on the third item? our schema is strict and we want to avoid silent failures if model changes fields. (2) can Redwood avoid returning partial objects mid-stream?

eng_ml_raj: on `metadata`: we recently onboarded a model variant that may add optional fields for provenance/heuristics. Best practice is to declare `additionalProperties: true` or mark `metadata` as optional in your schema, or validate keys per-item and ignore unknown keys. For stricter guarantees, include an explicit schema in the prompt that states unknown keys MUST be omitted, e.g. include this in the prompt: `Please only emit JSON matching EXACTLY the schema: {items:[{id:string,name:string,value:number}]}` — that reduces but doesn't eliminate model drift.

eng_runtime_lee: regarding avoiding partial objects: we can look into stronger chunk framing on our side (add boundaries or ensure streaming emits whole JSON tokens where possible), but it's non-trivial with low-latency streaming. I've flagged this to the runtime team; for now please use `stream=false` when you require strict JSON parsing, or implement reassembly logic. We'll open an internal ticket to investigate framing improvements.

billing_maria: tagging in case this impacts SLAs for dedicated customers — if you want guaranteed complete responses we should discuss Dedicated options where we can provide stronger service guarantees and custom runtime config.

acme_integration: appreciated. We'll add buffering to reassemble chunks and loosen the schema to allow optional `metadata` for now. Please open the ticket and keep me posted on runtime framing improvements. Request id again: req_20230212_9f3b.

support_jess: I've created internal ticket RED-INC-2023-113 and assigned to eng-runtime (lee) and eng-ml (raj). I'll follow up in-thread when we have a patch or workaround. Sorry for the disruption — let us know if you want a temporary Dedicated trial to avoid this in prod. :thumbsup:
